qti-assessment-test.title: CEimpact - Pharmacy Immunization Legal Authority, VIS/VAERS & Administration CPE (Self-Study Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply federal NCVIA (42 U.S.C. 300aa-26) Vaccine Information Statement timing and permanent recordkeeping rules to adult pharmacy immunizations.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Apply federal NCVIA (42 U.S.C. 300aa-26) Vaccine Information Statement timing and permanent recordkeeping rules to adult pharmacy immunizations.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A 54-year-old patient arrives at an outpatient pharmacy for a tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap) booster under a physician-signed statewide standing order. Which workflow satisfies federal National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act (NCVIA) compliance requirements?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Deliver the current CDC Tdap VIS before administering the vaccine, and record the VIS publication date, date given, vaccine manufacturer, lot number, and administering pharmacist's name and business address in the permanent record.
Omit the VIS because NCVIA applies only to pediatric patients under age 18, and provide the manufacturer's FDA package insert instead.
Obtain a federally mandated patient signature on the VIS copy and mail the signed sheet to NABP CPE Monitor within 72 hours.
Email the VIS link 24 hours after administration once the state Immunization Information System (IIS) confirms registry upload.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Under 42 U.S.C. 300aa-26, NCVIA VIS delivery prior to vaccination and permanent documentation of VIS edition/delivery dates, lot/manufacturer, and provider identity apply to every patient (adult or child) receiving a Vaccine Injury Table vaccine.
Incorrect. Despite the statute's title, NCVIA mandates pre-vaccination VIS delivery to adults as well whenever the antigen appears on the federal Vaccine Injury Table.
Incorrect. Federal NCVIA law does not require a patient signature on the VIS (unless required by state rule or payer policy), and patient records are never sent to NABP CPE Monitor.
Incorrect. 42 U.S.C. 300aa-26 strictly requires providing the current VIS prior to administering each vaccine dose.

qti-assessment-item.title: Select CDC ACIP-compliant needle length, injection angle, and deltoid anatomical landmarks to prevent SIRVA during adult intramuscular vaccination.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Select CDC ACIP-compliant needle length, injection angle, and deltoid anatomical landmarks to prevent SIRVA during adult intramuscular vaccination.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An immunizing pharmacist prepares to administer lyophilized recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) after reconstitution to a 62-year-old woman weighing 218 lb (99 kg). According to CDC ACIP General Best Practice Guidelines, which administration technique minimizes Shoulder Injury Related to Vaccine Administration (SIRVA) while ensuring intramuscular deposition?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Insert a 5/8-inch, 25-gauge needle at a 45-degree angle into the upper third of the deltoid 1 fingerbreadth below the acromion.
Administer RZV subcutaneously over the posterior triceps using a 5/8-inch needle to avoid deltoid soreness.
Insert a 1.5-inch, 22-to-25 gauge needle at a 90-degree angle into the central, thickest portion of the deltoid muscle 2 to 3 fingerbreadths below the acromion process.
Aspirate the plunger for 10 seconds inside the dorsogluteal muscle using a 1-inch needle.

qti-content-body.p: Incorrect. Injecting too high (near the acromion) risks piercing the subdeltoid bursa (causing SIRVA), and a 5/8-inch needle at 45 degrees fails to reach deltoid muscle tissue in a 218-lb adult, increasing local reactogenicity and reducing immunogenicity.
Incorrect. Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) is licensed exclusively for intramuscular administration; subcutaneous administration is a vaccine administration error.

Correct. CDC ACIP guidelines specify a 1.5-inch needle for women weighing over 200 lb (90 kg) inserted at 90 degrees into the central deltoid 2 to 3 fingerbreadths below the acromion to prevent subacromial bursa injury and subcutaneous under-penetration.
Incorrect. Neither the dorsogluteal site (sciatic nerve/adipose risk) nor syringe aspiration is recommended by CDC ACIP for routine immunizations.

qti-assessment-item.title: Execute emergency pharmacotherapy and federal VAERS reporting for post-vaccination anaphylaxis in the community pharmacy.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Execute emergency pharmacotherapy and federal VAERS reporting for post-vaccination anaphylaxis in the community pharmacy.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Nine minutes after receiving quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine, a 39-year-old adult develops diffuse flushing, hoarse stridor, wheezing, and blood pressure of 84/50 mmHg in the pharmacy waiting area. Which immediate intervention sequence aligns with CDC ACIP emergency protocols and federal reporting law?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Administer oral diphenhydramine 50 mg first, observe upright for 20 minutes, and reserve epinephrine unless cardiac arrest occurs.

Place the patient supine (unless respiratory distress dictates comfort), immediately inject intramuscular epinephrine 1 mg/mL (0.3 to 0.5 mg) into the mid-outer thigh, call 911, repeat epinephrine every 5 to 15 minutes if needed, and submit a mandatory VAERS report.
Inject 1 mL of 0.1 mg/mL (1:10,000) intravenous cardiac epinephrine rapidly into the deltoid vaccine site to slow antigen absorption.
Administer inhaled albuterol alone and withhold VAERS filing until an allergist confirms IgE-mediated causation.

qti-content-body.p: Incorrect. H1 antihistamines relieve pruritus/urticaria only and do not reverse life-threatening laryngeal edema, bronchospasm, or distributive shock; delaying epinephrine increases fatality risk, and upright posture risks empty-ventricle syndrome.

Correct. Intramuscular 1 mg/mL epinephrine into the anterolateral thigh (vastus lateralis) is mandatory first-line therapy for anaphylaxis alongside supine positioning, 911 EMS activation, and mandatory VAERS reporting under the VAERS Table.

Incorrect. Rapidly injecting cardiac IV dilutions or infiltrating the deltoid site instead of standard 1 mg/mL intramuscular vastus lateralis dosing delays peak plasma epinephrine levels and risks dosing errors.
Incorrect. Albuterol does not reverse upper-airway mucosal edema or hypotension, and VAERS mandates reporting post-vaccination anaphylaxis regardless of confirmed causation.
